vo.text: Eleven thirty on a bridge site. Pile seven hits rock at four metres. The soil report promised sand down to nine. That's a claim worth real money, if someone proves it today.
The proof sits in voice notes, photos and emails. It never reaches the office. BauBuddy changes that: talk on site, get the formal notice, with a source behind every field.
Local Whisper transcribes it. Claude extracts the fields and drafts the Nachtragsmeldung.
Every value cites its evidence. This one, page fourteen of the client's soil report. That one, row seven of the foreman's drilling list.
Nothing is guessed. A required detail has no source, so the field stays empty and BauBuddy asks. One answer, and it's filled.
The site manager checks it. Only that click releases it, as a Word file with an evidence appendix for the office.
And the AI site manager watches the whole site: which piles fall behind, where, and why, every finding linked to its source.

Under the hood: voice, photos, emails and schedule rows become evidence chunks with stable IDs. Claude proposes each field, but code enforces the rules: no valid citation or low confidence means no value. Computed values come from Python, and personal data is masked before any model sees it.
On new builds, six percent of building cost runs through Nachträge. BauBuddy makes sure they're filed, with proof, on time. We're Team Apex.

dictation.de: Pfahl sieben: um elf Uhr dreißig bei vier Meter auf Fels gestoßen, laut Baugrundgutachten erst ab neun Meter erwartet. Bohrzeit sechs Stunden statt zwei.
dictation.sub: 🇩🇪 “Pile 7: hit rock at 4 m at 11:30, the soil report expected it only from 9 m. Drilling took 6 hours instead of 2.”
